Fairness Metrics

Three standard tests, applied to the denial rate of genuine visits:

  • Disparity ratio: a group's denial rate divided by the best group's rate (1.0 = equal).
  • Four-fifths rule, adapted to failures: the classic rule flags a group whose success rate is below 80% of the best group's. For failure rates we flip it: a group FAILS if its denial rate is more than 1.25x (= 1 / 0.8) the best group's.
  • Chi-square test: is denial independent of the attribute? A p-value below 0.05 means the differences are unlikely to be chance.

The best (reference) group must have at least 30 visits so a tiny group cannot set the benchmark.

Reset Showing all data

Age group

GroupVisitsDenial rate Disparity ratioFour-fifths rule
18-30 (best) 1,573 1.3% 1.00x PASS
31-45 1,742 2.3% 1.81x FAIL
46-60 1,635 2.5% 1.97x FAIL
61-75 750 7.2% 5.66x FAIL
75+ 184 21.7% 17.10x FAIL

Chi-square p-value: < 0.001 (significant at 0.05)

People aged 75+ are 17.1 times more likely to be denied than people aged 18-30 (21.7% vs 1.3% of visits).

Chi-square p-value: < 0.001 (significant at 0.05)

People in the 'Farmer' group are 54.4 times more likely to be denied than people in the 'Office/Skilled' group (5.8% vs 0.1% of visits). (The best group is denied very rarely, which makes ratios large.)

Fairness Metrics

Three standard tests, applied to the denial rate of genuine visits:

  • Disparity ratio: a group's denial rate divided by the best group's rate (1.0 = equal).
  • Four-fifths rule, adapted to failures: the classic rule flags a group whose success rate is below 80% of the best group's. For failure rates we flip it: a group FAILS if its denial rate is more than 1.25x (= 1 / 0.8) the best group's.
  • Chi-square test: is denial independent of the attribute? A p-value below 0.05 means the differences are unlikely to be chance.

The best (reference) group must have at least 30 visits so a tiny group cannot set the benchmark.

  • Chi-square test: is denial independent of the attribute? A p-value below 0.05 means the differences are unlikely to be chance.

The best (reference) group must have at least 30 visits so a tiny group cannot set the benchmark.

Three standard tests, applied to the denial rate of genuine visits:

  • Disparity ratio: a group's denial rate divided by the best group's rate (1.0 = equal).
  • Four-fifths rule, adapted to failures: the classic rule flags a group whose success rate is below 80% of the best group's. For failure rates we flip it: a group FAILS if its denial rate is more than 1.25x (= 1 / 0.8) the best group's.
  • Chi-square test: is denial independent of the attribute? A p-value below 0.05 means the differences are unlikely to be chance.

The best (reference) group must have at least 30 visits so a tiny group cannot set the benchmark.
